celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَاعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ﴾ affirm His oneness ﴿وَلَا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا وَ﴾ do good ﴿بِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا﴾ dutifulness and gentleness ﴿وَبِذِي الْقُرْبَى﴾ kinship ﴿وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَالْجَارِ ذِي الْقُرْبَى﴾ the one near to you in neighbourhood or lineage ﴿وَالْجَارِ الْجُنُبِ﴾ the one far from you in neighbourhood or lineage ﴿وَالصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنْبِ﴾ the companion on a journey or in a trade; and it is said: the wife ﴿وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ the one stranded on his journey ﴿وَمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ of the slaves ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَنْ كَانَ مُخْتَالًا﴾ arrogant ﴿فَخُورًا﴾ boasting over people about what he has been given

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿يَبْخَلُونَ﴾ with what is obligatory upon them ﴿وَيَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبُخْلِ﴾ with it ﴿وَيَكْتُمُونَ مَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ of knowledge and wealth — and they are the Jews; and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is "for them is a severe threat" ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ in that and in other things ﴿عَذَابًا مُهِينًا﴾ possessing humiliation.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the الَّذِينَ before it ﴿يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ﴾ showing off to them ﴿وَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا بِالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ like the hypocrites and the people of Mecca ﴿وَمَنْ يَكُنِ الشَّيْطَانُ لَهُ قَرِينًا﴾ a companion whose command he acts upon, like these ﴿فَسَاءَ﴾ evil is ﴿قَرِينًا﴾ he

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿وَمَاذَا عَلَيْهِمْ لَوْ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَأَنْفَقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. what harm would there be to them in that? The question is for denial (inkār), and لَوْ is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar, verbal noun), i.e. there is no harm in it; the harm lies only in what they are upon ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِهِمْ عَلِيمًا﴾ so He will requite them for what they did

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ﴾ anyone ﴿مِثْقَالَ﴾ the weight of ﴿ذَرَّةٍ﴾ the smallest ant, by decreasing it from his good deeds or adding it to his evil deeds ﴿وَإِنْ تَكُ﴾ the ذَرَّة ﴿حَسَنَةً﴾ from a believer — and in one reading it is in the nominative (marfūʿ), so كان is complete (tāmma) ﴿يُضَاعِفْهَا﴾ from ten to more than seven hundred — and in one reading [يُضَعِّفْهَا] with doubling (tashdīd) ﴿وَيُؤْتِ مِنْ لَدُنْهُ﴾ from Him, together with the multiplying ﴿أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ which no one can measure

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ will be the state of the disbelievers ﴿إِذَا جِئْنَا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ﴾ who testifies against it about its deeds, and he is its prophet ﴿وَجِئْنَا بِكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿عَلَى هَؤُلَاءِ شَهِيدًا﴾

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ the day of the coming ﴿يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَعَصَوُا الرَّسُولَ لَوْ﴾ i.e. أَنْ ﴿تُسَوَّى﴾ with the passive form, and with the active form with omission of one of the two tāʾs in the original, and with its assimilation (idghām) into the sīn, i.e. تَتَسَوَّى ﴿بِهِمُ الْأَرْضُ﴾ by their becoming dust like it, because of the greatness of its terror, as in another ayah: {وَيَقُولُ الْكَافِرُ يَا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُرَابًا} ﴿وَلَا يَكْتُمُونَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثًا﴾ of what they did; and at another time they conceal it and say {وَاللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ}

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلَاةَ﴾ i.e. do not pray ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ سُكَارَى﴾ from drink, because the occasion of its revelation was a congregational prayer in a state of intoxication ﴿حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا مَا تَقُولُونَ﴾ by becoming sober ﴿وَلَا جُنُبًا﴾ through penetration or ejaculation; its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is applied to the singular and others ﴿إِلَّا عَابِرِي﴾ passing along ﴿سَبِيلٍ﴾ a road, i.e. travellers ﴿حَتَّى تَغْتَسِلُوا﴾ then you may pray. The traveller is excepted because he has another ruling which will come; and it is said that what is meant is the prohibition of approaching the places of prayer, i.e. the mosques, not passing through them without staying ﴿وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضَى﴾ with an illness which water harms ﴿أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ﴾ i.e. travelling while you are in a state of janāba or of minor impurity ﴿أَوْ جَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِنَ الْغَائِطِ﴾ it is the place prepared for relieving oneself, i.e. he has broken his ablution ﴿أَوْ لَامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ﴾ and in one reading without alif; and both mean touching (lams), which is feeling with the hand — Ibn ʿUmar said this, and al-Shāfiʿī holds it, and feeling with the rest of the skin is joined to it; and from Ibn ʿAbbās: it is intercourse ﴿فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا مَاءً﴾ with which to purify yourselves for the prayer, after seeking and searching — and this goes back to all except the sick ﴿فَتَيَمَّمُوا﴾ aim for, after the time has entered ﴿صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا﴾ pure earth, and strike it twice ﴿فَامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكُمْ وَأَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ together with the elbows, with it; and مَسَحَ is transitive by itself and by the preposition ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا﴾

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيبًا﴾ a share ﴿مِنَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ and they are the Jews ﴿يَشْتَرُونَ الضَّلَالَةَ﴾ for guidance ﴿وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا السَّبِيلَ﴾ that you miss the true path, so that you become like them.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِأَعْدَائِكُمْ﴾ than you, so He informs you of them so that you avoid them ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ وَلِيًّا﴾ as a protector for you from them ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ نَصِيرًا﴾ as a defender of you from their plotting

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا﴾ there are people who ﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ﴾ alter ﴿الْكَلِمَ﴾ which Allah revealed in the Torah, of the description of Muhammad ﷺ ﴿عَنْ مَوَاضِعِهِ﴾ upon which it was placed ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ to the Prophet ﷺ when he commanded them with something ﴿سَمِعْنَا﴾ your words ﴿وَعَصَيْنَا﴾ your command ﴿وَاسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of an imprecation, i.e. "may you not hear" ﴿وَ﴾ they say to him ﴿رَاعِنَا﴾ — addressing him with it had been forbidden, and it is a word of insult in their language ﴿لَيًّا﴾ a distortion ﴿بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ وَطَعْنًا﴾ a disparagement ﴿فِي الدِّينِ﴾ Islam ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا﴾ instead of وَعَصَيْنَا ﴿وَاسْمَعْ﴾ only ﴿وَانْظُرْنَا﴾ look at us, instead of رَاعِنَا ﴿لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ﴾ than what they said ﴿وَأَقْوَمَ﴾ more just than it ﴿وَلَكِنْ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ He removed them far from His mercy ﴿بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ of them, like ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and his companions

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ آمِنُوا بِمَا نَزَّلْنَا﴾ of the Quran ﴿مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا مَعَكُمْ﴾ of the Torah ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَطْمِسَ وُجُوهًا﴾ We wipe out what is in them of the eye, the nose and the eyebrow ﴿فَنَرُدَّهَا عَلَى أَدْبَارِهَا﴾ and make them like the napes, a single flat surface ﴿أَوْ نَلْعَنَهُمْ﴾ We transform them into apes ﴿كَمَا لَعَنَّا﴾ We transformed ﴿أَصْحَابَ السَّبْتِ﴾ among them ﴿وَكَانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ His decree ﴿مَفْعُولًا﴾. When it was revealed, ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām embraced Islam. It is said it was a conditional threat, so when some of them embraced Islam it was lifted; and it is said there will be an effacing and transformation before the coming of the Hour

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ﴾ i.e. associating partners ﴿بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ﴾ other than ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ of sins ﴿لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ forgiveness for, by admitting him into Paradise without punishment; and whomever of the believers He wills He punishes for his sins and then admits him into Paradise ﴿وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدِ افْتَرَى إِثْمًا﴾ a sin ﴿عَظِيمًا﴾ great

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ and they are the Jews, when they said: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved," i.e. the matter is not by their purifying themselves ﴿بَلِ اللَّهُ يُزَكِّي﴾ purifies ﴿مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ by faith ﴿وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ they will not be shortchanged of their deeds ﴿فَتِيلًا﴾ the measure of the skin of a date-stone

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿انْظُرْ﴾ in wonder ﴿كَيْفَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ﴾ by that ﴿وَكَفَى بِهِ إِثْمًا مُبِينًا﴾ clear. And it was revealed about Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and those like him among the scholars of the Jews, when they came to Mecca, saw the slain of Badr, and incited the idolaters to take their revenge and to wage war on the Prophet ﷺ

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الْكِتَابِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْجِبْتِ وَالطَّاغُوتِ﴾ two idols of Quraysh ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ Abū Sufyān and his companions, when they said to them: "Are we better guided in way — we are custodians, we give water to the pilgrims, entertain the guest, free the captive, and do [such things] — or Muhammad, who has opposed the religion of his forefathers, cut the ties of kinship and left the Sanctuary?" ﴿هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ i.e. you ﴿أَهْدَى مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا سَبِيلًا﴾ more upright in path.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ وَمَنْ يَلْعَنِ﴾ him [هُ] ﴿اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ نَصِيرًا﴾ a defender from His punishment

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ rather, is it that [بَلْ أَ] ﴿لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُلْكِ﴾ i.e. they have nothing of it; and if they had ﴿فَإِذًا لَا يُؤْتُونَ النَّاسَ نَقِيرًا﴾ i.e. a paltry thing, the measure of the speck on the back of a date-stone, because of the excess of their miserliness

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ rather, is it that [بَلْ أَ] ﴿يَحْسُدُونَ النَّاسَ﴾ i.e. the Prophet ﷺ ﴿عَلَى مَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ of prophethood and many wives, i.e. they wish for it to be removed from him, and they say: "If he were a prophet, he would be too busy for women" ﴿فَقَدْ آتَيْنَا آلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ his forefather, such as Moses, David and Solomon ﴿الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ﴾ and prophethood ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُمْ مُلْكًا عَظِيمًا﴾ for David had ninety-nine wives, and Solomon a thousand, between free women and concubines

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ﴾ in Muhammad ﷺ ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ صَدَّ﴾ turned away ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ and did not believe ﴿وَكَفَى بِجَهَنَّمَ سَعِيرًا﴾ as punishment for whoever does not believe

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِنَا سَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِمْ﴾ We will enter them into ﴿نَارًا﴾ in which they burn ﴿كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ﴾ is burnt ﴿جُلُودُهُمْ بَدَّلْنَاهُمْ جُلُودًا غَيْرَهَا﴾ by its being returned to its first state, unburnt ﴿لِيَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ﴾ so that they suffer its severity ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَزِيزًا﴾ nothing incapacitates Him ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in His creation

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا لَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ﴾ from menstruation and every impurity ﴿وَنُدْخِلُهُمْ ظِلًّا ظَلِيلًا﴾ lasting, which no sun dispels — it is the shade of Paradise

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ﴾ i.e. the rights one has been entrusted with ﴿إِلَى أَهْلِهَا﴾ It was revealed when ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, took the key of the Kaʿba by force from ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥa al-Ḥajabī, its custodian, when the Prophet ﷺ came to Mecca in the year of the Conquest. He had withheld it and said: "Had I known that he is the Messenger of Allah, I would not have withheld it." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered it to be returned to him and said: "Take it, perpetual and ancestral." He was amazed at that, so ʿAlī recited the ayah to him and he embraced Islam; and at his death he gave it to his brother Shayba, and it remained among his descendants. And the ayah, even though it came about a specific occasion, its generality is taken into account, by the indication of the plural ﴿وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ﴾ He commands you ﴿أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا بِالْعَدْلِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ نِعِمَّا﴾ in it there is assimilation (idghām) of the mīm of نِعْمَ into مَا, the indefinite described [noun], i.e. "an excellent thing" ﴿يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ﴾ the rendering of the trust and judging with justice ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ سَمِيعًا﴾ of what is said ﴿بَصِيرًا﴾ of what is done

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَأُولِي﴾ the possessors of ﴿الْأَمْرِ﴾ i.e. the rulers ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ when they command you with obedience to Allah and His Messenger ﴿فَإِنْ تَنَازَعْتُمْ﴾ you differ ﴿فِي شَيْءٍ فَرُدُّوهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. to His Book ﴿وَالرَّسُولِ﴾ during his lifetime, and after him to his Sunna, i.e. uncover it from the two of them ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. referring back to them ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ for you than disputing and speaking by opinion ﴿وَأَحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلًا﴾ outcome.

celaleyn:60-60.t: And it was revealed when a Jew and a hypocrite disputed: [the hypocrite] called for Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf to judge between them, and the Jew called for the Prophet ﷺ. So they came to him and he judged in favour of the Jew, but the hypocrite was not satisfied. They then came to ʿUmar, and the Jew mentioned that, so he said to the hypocrite: "Is it so?" He said: "Yes," so he killed him. ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَتَحَاكَمُوا إِلَى الطَّاغُوتِ﴾ the one of much transgression, and he is Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf ﴿وَقَدْ أُمِرُوا أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا بِهِ﴾ and not take him as an ally ﴿وَيُرِيدُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَنْ يُضِلَّهُمْ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ from the truth

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْا إِلَى مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ in the Quran of judgement ﴿وَإِلَى الرَّسُولِ﴾ so that he judges between you ﴿رَأَيْتَ الْمُنَافِقِينَ يَصُدُّونَ﴾ turning away ﴿عَنْكَ﴾ to someone other than you ﴿صُدُودًا﴾

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ will they do ﴿إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ﴾ a punishment ﴿بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ of disbelief and sins, i.e. will they be able to turn away and flee from it? No ﴿ثُمَّ جَاءُوكَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يَصُدُّونَ ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ إِنْ﴾ not [مَا] ﴿أَرَدْنَا﴾ by seeking judgement from someone other than you ﴿إِلَّا إِحْسَانًا﴾ reconciliation ﴿وَتَوْفِيقًا﴾ bringing the two disputants together by approximation in judgement, rather than forcing [them] to the bitterness of the truth

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ of hypocrisy, and their lying in their excuse ﴿فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ by pardoning ﴿وَعِظْهُمْ﴾ make them fear Allah ﴿وَقُلْ لَهُمْ فِي﴾ the matter of ﴿أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَوْلًا بَلِيغًا﴾ having effect upon them, i.e. rebuke them so that they turn back from their disbelief

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا لِيُطَاعَ﴾ in what he commands and judges ﴿بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His command, not to be disobeyed and opposed ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ إِذْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ by seeking judgement from the ṭāghūt ﴿جَاءُوكَ﴾ repenting ﴿فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا اللَّهَ وَاسْتَغْفَرَ لَهُمُ الرَّسُولُ﴾ in it there is a shift (iltifāt) away from the second person, to magnify his standing ﴿لَوَجَدُوا اللَّهَ تَوَّابًا﴾ toward them ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to them

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ﴾ لَا is redundant (zāʾida) ﴿لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّى يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ﴾ became entangled ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجًا﴾ tightness or doubt ﴿مِمَّا قَضَيْتَ﴾ with ﴿وَيُسَلِّمُوا﴾ submit to your judgement ﴿تَسْلِيمًا﴾ without opposition.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّا كَتَبْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَنِ﴾ explicative (mufassira) ﴿اقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ أَوِ اخْرُجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِكُمْ﴾ as We prescribed for the Children of Israel ﴿مَا فَعَلُوهُ﴾ i.e. what was prescribed for them ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ﴾ in the nominative as a badal (substitute), and in the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā) ﴿مِنْهُمْ وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ فَعَلُوا مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِ﴾ of obedience to the Messenger ﴿لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ تَثْبِيتًا﴾ a realisation of their faith

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿وَإِذًا﴾ i.e. if they were firm ﴿لَآتَيْنَاهُمْ مِنْ لَدُنَّا﴾ from Us ﴿أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ it is Paradise

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿وَلَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ صِرَاطًا مُسْتَقِيمًا﴾ One of the Companions said to the Prophet ﷺ: "How will we see you in Paradise, when you are in the highest ranks and we are below you?" So [the following] was revealed

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ﴾ in what he commanded ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ﴾ the most excellent of the companions of the prophets, because of their intensity in truthfulness and affirming the truth ﴿وَالشُّهَدَاءِ﴾ those slain in the way of Allah ﴿وَالصَّالِحِينَ﴾ other than those mentioned ﴿وَحَسُنَ أُولَئِكَ رَفِيقًا﴾ companions in Paradise, in that one enjoys seeing them, visiting them and being present with them there, even if their abode is in the high ranks relative to others

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. their being with those mentioned; a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿الْفَضْلُ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ He bestowed it upon them as a favour, not that they attained it by their acts of obedience ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ عَلِيمًا﴾ of the reward of the Hereafter, i.e. so trust in what He has informed you of: {وَلَا يُنَبِّئُكَ مِثْلُ خَبِيرٍ}

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا خُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ﴾ from your enemy, i.e. guard yourselves against him and be alert to him ﴿فَانْفِرُوا﴾ rise up to fight him ﴿ثُبَاتٍ﴾ scattered, one detachment after another ﴿أَوِ انْفِرُوا جَمِيعًا﴾ gathered together

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَنْ لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ﴾ who will surely lag behind from fighting, like ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy the hypocrite and his companions; He made him one of them in terms of outward appearance; and the lām in the verb is for the oath ﴿فَإِنْ أَصَابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ﴾ such as killing and defeat ﴿قَالَ قَدْ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ إِذْ لَمْ أَكُنْ مَعَهُمْ شَهِيدًا﴾ present, so that I would be struck

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the lām of oath ﴿أَصَابَكُمْ فَضْلٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ such as victory and spoils ﴿لَيَقُولَنَّ﴾ regretfully ﴿كَأَنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa), and its noun is omitted, i.e. كَأَنَّهُ ﴿لَمْ يَكُنْ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [لَمْ تَكُنْ] ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُ مَوَدَّةٌ﴾ acquaintance and friendship — and this goes back to his saying قَدْ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ; it was interposed between the saying and what is said, which is ﴿يَا﴾ for calling attention ﴿لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ مَعَهُمْ فَأَفُوزَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا﴾ I would take an ample share of the spoils. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿فَلْيُقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ to make His religion supreme ﴿الَّذِينَ يَشْرُونَ﴾ sell ﴿الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا بِالْآخِرَةِ وَمَنْ يُقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَيُقْتَلْ﴾ is martyred ﴿أَوْ يَغْلِبْ﴾ triumphs over his enemy ﴿فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ an abundant reward.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ لَا تُقَاتِلُونَ﴾ a question of rebuke, i.e. nothing prevents you from fighting ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَ﴾ in rescuing ﴿الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ وَالْوِلْدَانِ﴾ whom the disbelievers held back from emigration and harmed. Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "My mother and I were among them." ﴿الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ﴾ supplicating: O [يَا] ﴿رَبَّنَا أَخْرِجْنَا مِنْ هَذِهِ الْقَرْيَةِ﴾ Mecca ﴿الظَّالِمِ أَهْلُهَا﴾ by disbelief ﴿وَاجْعَلْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ﴾ from You ﴿وَلِيًّا﴾ who takes charge of our affairs ﴿وَاجْعَلْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ نَصِيرًا﴾ who protects us from them. And Allah answered their supplication: He made leaving easy for some of them, and some remained until Mecca was conquered and he ﷺ appointed ʿAttāb ibn Asīd [governor], who gave their wronged ones justice against their wrongdoers

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ الطَّاغُوتِ﴾ Satan ﴿فَقَاتِلُوا أَوْلِيَاءَ الشَّيْطَانِ﴾ the helpers of his religion; you will overcome them through your strength in Allah ﴿إِنَّ كَيْدَ الشَّيْطَانِ﴾ against the believers ﴿كَانَ ضَعِيفًا﴾ feeble, not withstanding Allah's plan against the disbelievers

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمْ كُفُّوا أَيْدِيَكُمْ﴾ from fighting the disbelievers, when they requested it in Mecca because of the disbelievers' harm to them — and they were a group of the Companions ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَوةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ﴾ was made obligatory ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ الْقِتَالُ إِذَا فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ يَخْشَوْنَ﴾ fear ﴿النَّاسَ﴾ the disbelievers, i.e. their punishing them by killing ﴿كَخَشْيَةِ﴾ their [fear of] the punishment of [هِمْ عَذَابَ] ﴿اللَّهِ أَوْ أَشَدَّ خَشْيَةً﴾ than their fear of Him. The accusative of أَشَدَّ is as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the jawāb (apodosis) of لَمَّا is indicated by إِذَا and what follows it, i.e. "fear came upon them" ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ in alarm at death ﴿رَبَّنَا لِمَ كَتَبْتَ عَلَيْنَا الْقِتَالَ لَوْلَا﴾ why not ﴿أَخَّرْتَنَا إِلَى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿مَتَاعُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ what is enjoyed in it, or the enjoyment of it ﴿قَلِيلٌ﴾ heading to extinction ﴿وَالْآخِرَةُ﴾ i.e. Paradise ﴿خَيْرٌ لِمَنِ اتَّقَى﴾ Allah's punishment by abandoning disobedience to Him ﴿وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and yāʾ; you will not be shortchanged of your deeds ﴿فَتِيلًا﴾ the measure of the skin of a date-stone — so strive

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿أَيْنَ مَا تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكْكُمُ الْمَوْتُ وَلَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُرُوجٍ﴾ fortresses ﴿مُشَيَّدَةٍ﴾ lofty — so do not fear fighting out of fear of death ﴿وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿حَسَنَةٌ﴾ fertility and plenty ﴿يَقُولُوا هَذِهِ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ﴾ drought and affliction, as happened to them when the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina ﴿يَقُولُوا هَذِهِ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ﴾ O Muhammad, i.e. by your ill omen ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ of the good and the evil ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ﴾ from His side ﴿فَمَا لِهَؤُلَاءِ الْقَوْمِ لَا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ i.e. they do not come near to understanding ﴿حَدِيثًا﴾ which is put to them. مَا is a question expressing wonder at the excess of their ignorance, and negating nearness to the act is stronger than negating it

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿مَا أَصَابَكَ﴾ O human being ﴿مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ﴾ good ﴿فَمِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ came to you as a favour from Him ﴿وَمَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ سَيِّئَةٍ﴾ affliction ﴿فَمِنْ نَفْسِكَ﴾ came to you, since you committed sins that necessitate it ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَاكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿لِلنَّاسِ رَسُولًا﴾ an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida, emphasising circumstantial) ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا﴾ to your message.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿مَنْ يُطِعِ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدْ أَطَاعَ اللَّهَ وَمَنْ تَوَلَّى﴾ turns away from obeying him, then let it not concern you ﴿فَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظًا﴾ a keeper of their deeds, but rather a warner, and their affair is up to Us, so We will requite them. This was before the command to fight

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ i.e. the hypocrites, when they come to you: our affair is ﴿طَاعَةٌ﴾ to you ﴿فَإِذَا بَرَزُوا﴾ went out ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِكَ بَيَّتَ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ with assimilation (idghām) of the tāʾ into the ṭāʾ and without it, i.e. harboured ﴿غَيْرَ الَّذِي تَقُولُ﴾ to you in your presence of obedience, i.e. disobedience to you ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَكْتُبُ﴾ commands the recording of ﴿مَا يُبَيِّتُونَ﴾ in their records, so that they are requited for it ﴿فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ by pardoning ﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ trust in Him, for He suffices you ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا﴾ as one to whom [matters] are entrusted

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ﴾ reflect on ﴿الْقُرْآنَ﴾ and the wondrous meanings in it ﴿وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا فِيهِ اخْتِلَافًا كَثِيرًا﴾ contradiction in its meanings and disparity in its composition

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿وَإِذَا جَاءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ﴾ about the expeditions of the Prophet ﷺ, of what befell them ﴿مِنَ الْأَمْنِ﴾ by victory ﴿أَوِ الْخَوْفِ﴾ by defeat ﴿أَذَاعُوا بِهِ﴾ they spread it. It was revealed about a group of the hypocrites, or about weak believers, who used to do that, so the hearts of the believers would weaken and the Prophet would be hurt ﴿وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ﴾ i.e. the news ﴿إِلَى الرَّسُولِ وَإِلَى أُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the people of sound judgement among the senior Companions; i.e. had they kept silent about it until they [the Messenger and those in authority] informed of it ﴿لَعَلِمَهُ﴾ whether it is something that should be spread or not ﴿الَّذِينَ يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ﴾ follow it up and seek knowledge of it — and they are those who spread it ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ from the Messenger and those in authority ﴿وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ through Islam ﴿وَرَحْمَتُهُ﴾ to you through the Quran ﴿لَاتَّبَعْتُمُ الشَّيْطَانَ﴾ in the indecencies he commands you to ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿فَقَاتِلْ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَا تُكَلَّفُ إِلَّا نَفْسَكَ﴾ so do not be troubled by their staying behind from you. The meaning: fight, even if alone, for you are promised victory ﴿وَحَرِّضِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ urge them to fight and make them desire it ﴿عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَكُفَّ بَأْسَ﴾ the warfare of ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَاللَّهُ أَشَدُّ بَأْسًا﴾ than they ﴿وَأَشَدُّ تَنْكِيلًا﴾ in punishment than they. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will go out even if alone." So he went out with seventy riders to the Lesser Badr, and Allah held back the might of the disbelievers by casting terror into their hearts and preventing Abū Sufyān from going out, as has preceded in Āl ʿImrān

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿مَنْ يَشْفَعْ﴾ between people ﴿شَفَاعَةً حَسَنَةً﴾ in accordance with the Sacred Law ﴿يَكُنْ لَهُ نَصِيبٌ﴾ of the reward ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ because of it ﴿وَمَنْ يَشْفَعْ شَفَاعَةً سَيِّئَةً﴾ contrary to it ﴿يَكُنْ لَهُ كِفْلٌ﴾ a share of the burden ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ because of it ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقِيتًا﴾ all-able, so He requites everyone for what he did

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُمْ بِتَحِيَّةٍ﴾ such as when it is said to you "سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ" ﴿فَحَيُّوا﴾ the one greeting ﴿بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَا﴾ by saying to him: "عَلَيْكَ السَّلَامُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ" ﴿أَوْ رُدُّوهَا﴾ by saying to him as he said; i.e. one of the two is obligatory, and the first is better ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَسِيبًا﴾ taking account, so He requites for it — and among that is returning the greeting. The Sunna has made exceptions for the disbeliever, the innovator, the open sinner, the one greeting someone relieving himself, the one in the bathhouse, and the one eating: returning [the greeting] to them is not obligatory; rather, it is disliked except for the last; and to the disbeliever one says: "وَعَلَيْكَ".

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ by Allah ﴿لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ﴾ from your graves ﴿إِلَى﴾ on ﴿يَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ لَا رَيْبَ﴾ doubt ﴿فِيهِ وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. no one ﴿أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حَدِيثًا﴾ in speech. When some people returned from Uḥud, people differed about them: one group said "Kill them," and another said "No," so [the following] was revealed

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿فَمَا لَكُمْ﴾ i.e. what is the matter with you that you have become ﴿فِي الْمُنَافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ﴾ two parties ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَرْكَسَهُمْ﴾ turned them back ﴿بِمَا كَسَبُوا﴾ of disbelief and sins ﴿أَتُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَهْدُوا مَنْ أَضَلَّ﴾ him [هُ] ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. count them among the rightly guided; and the question in both places is for denial (inkār) ﴿وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ﴾ him [هُ] ﴿اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ سَبِيلًا﴾ a path to guidance

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿وَدُّوا﴾ they wished ﴿لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ كَمَا كَفَرُوا فَتَكُونُونَ﴾ you and they ﴿سَوَاءً﴾ in disbelief ﴿فَلَا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ whom you befriend, even if they display faith ﴿حَتَّى يُهَاجِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ a sound emigration that confirms their faith ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ and persisted in what they are upon ﴿فَخُذُوهُمْ﴾ captive ﴿وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْهُمْ وَلِيًّا﴾ whom you befriend ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرًا﴾ by whom you are helped against your enemy

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ﴾ take refuge ﴿إِلَى قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثَاقٌ﴾ a covenant of safety for them and for whoever reaches them, as the Prophet ﷺ made a covenant with Hilāl ibn ʿUwaymir al-Aslamī ﴿أَوْ﴾ those who ﴿جَاءُوكُمْ﴾ while [قَدْ] ﴿حَصِرَتْ﴾ are constricted ﴿صُدُورُهُمْ﴾ from [عَنْ] ﴿أَنْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ﴾ together with their people ﴿أَوْ يُقَاتِلُوا قَوْمَهُمْ﴾ together with you, i.e. refraining from fighting you and fighting them; so do not interfere with them by capture or killing. This and what follows it is abrogated by the Ayah of the Sword ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ to give them power over you ﴿لَسَلَّطَهُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ by strengthening their hearts ﴿فَلَقَاتَلُوكُمْ﴾ but He did not will it, so He cast terror into their hearts ﴿فَإِنِ اعْتَزَلُوكُمْ فَلَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ وَأَلْقَوْا إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلَمَ﴾ peace, i.e. they submitted ﴿فَمَا جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way to capture and killing

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿سَتَجِدُونَ آخَرِينَ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَأْمَنُوكُمْ﴾ by displaying faith before you ﴿وَيَأْمَنُوا قَوْمَهُمْ﴾ by disbelief when they return to them — and they are Asad and Ghaṭafān ﴿كُلَّمَا رُدُّوا إِلَى الْفِتْنَةِ﴾ were called to idolatry ﴿أُرْكِسُوا فِيهَا﴾ they fell into it most completely ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يَعْتَزِلُوكُمْ﴾ by abandoning fighting you ﴿وَ﴾ do not [لَمْ] ﴿يُلْقُوا إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلَمَ وَ﴾ do not [لَمْ] ﴿يَكُفُّوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾ from you ﴿فَخُذُوهُمْ﴾ captive ﴿وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ you find them ﴿وَأُولَئِكُمْ جَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَانًا مُبِينًا﴾ a clear, manifest proof for killing and capturing them, because of their treachery.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَنْ يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِنًا﴾ i.e. it is not fitting that killing him should issue from him ﴿إِلَّا خَطَأً﴾ erring in killing him, without intent ﴿وَمَنْ قَتَلَ مُؤْمِنًا خَطَأً﴾ by aiming to shoot something else, such as game or a tree, and hitting him, or striking him with something that does not usually kill ﴿فَتَحْرِيرُ﴾ the freeing of ﴿رَقَبَةٍ﴾ a soul ﴿مُؤْمِنَةٍ﴾ is upon him ﴿وَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ﴾ paid ﴿إِلَى أَهْلِهِ﴾ i.e. the heirs of the one killed ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَصَّدَّقُوا﴾ give it to him in charity by waiving it. The Sunna has made clear that it is a hundred camels: twenty bint makhāḍ (one-year-old females), and likewise [twenty each of] banāt labūn (two-year-old females), banū labūn (two-year-old males), ḥiqāq (three-year-olds) and jidhāʿ (four-year-olds); and that it is upon the ʿāqila (blood-money group) of the killer — they are his agnatic relatives, except ascendants and descendants — distributed among them over three years: upon the wealthy among them half a dīnār, and upon the middling a quarter, each year; if they do not cover it, then from the public treasury; and if that is not possible, then upon the offender ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَ﴾ the one killed ﴿مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَدُوٍّ﴾ at war ﴿لَكُمْ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ﴾ is upon his killer as an expiation, and no blood money is paid to his family because of their being at war ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ﴾ the one killed ﴿مِنْ قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثَاقٌ﴾ a covenant, like the protected people (ahl al-dhimma) ﴿فَدِيَةٌ﴾ for him ﴿مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ﴾ and it is a third of the blood money of a believer if he was a Jew or a Christian, and two-thirds of a tenth of it if he was a Magian ﴿وَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ﴾ is upon his killer ﴿فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ﴾ the slave, by lacking it and the means of obtaining it ﴿فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ﴾ is upon him as an expiation. Allah the Exalted did not mention moving on to feeding, as in ẓihār, and al-Shāfiʿī adopted this in the sounder of his two opinions ﴿تَوْبَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the accusative by its implied (muqaddar) verb ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in what He has arranged for them

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِنًا مُتَعَمِّدًا﴾ by intending to kill him with something that usually kills, knowing of his faith ﴿فَجَزَاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ خَالِدًا فِيهَا وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَلَعَنَهُ﴾ removed him far from His mercy ﴿وَأَعَدَّ لَهُ عَذَابًا عَظِيمًا﴾ in the Fire. This is interpreted as referring to one who deems it lawful, or [as meaning] that this is his recompense if he is recompensed; and there is nothing novel in the non-fulfilment of a threat, because of His saying {وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ}. And from Ibn ʿAbbās: that it is to be taken at its apparent meaning, and that it abrogates the other ayahs of forgiveness. The ayah of al-Baqara has made clear that the deliberate killer is killed for him, and that blood money is upon him if he is pardoned, and its amount has preceded. And the Sunna has made clear that between deliberate and mistaken there is a killing called "quasi-deliberate" (shibh al-ʿamd), which is killing him with something that does not usually kill; there is no retaliation in it, but rather blood money, like the deliberate in its description and like the mistaken in its deferral and its being borne [by the ʿāqila]; and it and the deliberate are more deserving of expiation than the mistaken. And [the following] was revealed when a group of the Companions passed by a man of Banū Sulaym who was driving sheep; he greeted them with salām, and they said: "He only greeted us out of fear (taqiyya)," so they killed him and drove off his sheep

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ﴾ travelled for jihad ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُوا﴾ — and in one reading with the thāʾ (with three dots) in both places ﴿وَلَا تَقُولُوا لِمَنْ أَلْقَى إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامَ﴾ with alif or without it, i.e. the greeting, or submission by the word of testimony, which is a sign of Islam ﴿لَسْتَ مُؤْمِنًا﴾ "you only said this out of fear for yourself and your property," and so kill him ﴿تَبْتَغُونَ﴾ seeking by that ﴿عَرَضَ الْحَيَوةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ its goods, of booty ﴿فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَغَانِمُ كَثِيرَةٌ﴾ which make you independent of killing such a one for his property ﴿كَذَلِكَ كُنْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ your blood and property were protected merely by your saying the testimony ﴿فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ by becoming well known for faith and uprightness ﴿فَتَبَيَّنُوا﴾ lest you kill a believer, and do with one entering Islam as was done with you ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ so He will requite you for it.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿لَا يَسْتَوِي الْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ from jihad ﴿غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ﴾ in the nominative as an adjective (ṣifa), and in the accusative as an exception — such as chronic illness, blindness and the like ﴿وَالْمُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ الْمُجَاهِدِينَ بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ عَلَى الْقَاعِدِينَ﴾ because of an impediment ﴿دَرَجَةً﴾ a merit, since they are equal in intention and the strivers have more by actually doing it ﴿وَكُلًّا﴾ of the two groups ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنَى﴾ Paradise ﴿وَفَضَّلَ اللَّهُ الْمُجَاهِدِينَ عَلَى الْقَاعِدِينَ﴾ without an impediment ﴿أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ and a badal (substitute) is made from it:

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿دَرَجَاتٍ مِنْهُ﴾ stations of honour, one above another ﴿وَمَغْفِرَةً وَرَحْمَةً﴾ both in the accusative by their implied (muqaddar) verbs ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا﴾ to His friends ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to the people of obedience to Him. And [the following] was revealed about a group who embraced Islam but did not emigrate, and were killed on the day of Badr with the disbelievers

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ by staying with the disbelievers and abandoning emigration ﴿قَالُوا﴾ to them in rebuke ﴿فِيمَ كُنْتُمْ﴾ i.e. in what state were you regarding the matter of your religion ﴿قَالُوا﴾ apologising ﴿كُنَّا مُسْتَضْعَفِينَ﴾ unable to establish the religion ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the land of Mecca ﴿قَالُوا﴾ to them in rebuke ﴿أَلَمْ تَكُنْ أَرْضُ اللَّهِ وَاسِعَةً فَتُهَاجِرُوا فِيهَا﴾ from the land of disbelief to another land, as others did. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَسَاءَتْ مَصِيرًا﴾ it is

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿إِلَّا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ وَالْوِلْدَانِ﴾ who ﴿لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً﴾ have no strength for emigration nor means ﴿وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا﴾ a road to the land of emigration

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَعْفُوَ عَنْهُمْ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يُهَاجِرْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يَجِدْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُرَاغَمًا﴾ a place of emigration ﴿كَثِيرًا وَسَعَةً﴾ in provision ﴿وَمَنْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِرًا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ﴾ on the way, as happened to Jundaʿ ibn Ḍamra al-Laythī ﴿فَقَدْ وَقَعَ﴾ is established ﴿أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿وَإِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ﴾ travel ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ﴾ in [فِي] ﴿أَنْ تَقْصُرُوا مِنَ الصَّلَوةِ﴾ by reducing it from four to two ﴿إِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنَكُمْ﴾ i.e. afflict you with something hateful ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ — an explanation of what was the case at that time, so it has no implied converse meaning (mafhūm). The Sunna has made clear that what is meant by travel is the long [journey], which is four barīds, which is two stages; and it is taken from His saying {فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ} that it is a concession, not an obligation — and al-Shāfiʿī holds this ﴿إِنَّ الْكَافِرِينَ كَانُوا لَكُمْ عَدُوًّا مُبِينًا﴾ clear in enmity.

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿وَإِذَا كُنْتَ﴾ O Muhammad, present ﴿فِيهِمْ﴾ while you fear the enemy ﴿فَأَقَمْتَ لَهُمُ الصَّلَوةَ﴾ — this follows the custom of the Quran in address, so it has no implied converse meaning (mafhūm) ﴿فَلْتَقُمْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ مَعَكَ﴾ and let a group stay back ﴿وَلْيَأْخُذُوا﴾ i.e. the group that stood with you ﴿أَسْلِحَتَهُمْ﴾ with them ﴿فَإِذَا سَجَدُوا﴾ i.e. prayed ﴿فَلْيَكُونُوا﴾ i.e. the other group ﴿مِنْ وَرَائِكُمْ﴾ guarding until you complete the prayer, and this group goes to guard ﴿وَلْتَأْتِ طَائِفَةٌ أُخْرَى لَمْ يُصَلُّوا فَلْيُصَلُّوا مَعَكَ وَلْيَأْخُذُوا حِذْرَهُمْ وَأَسْلِحَتَهُمْ﴾ with them until you complete the prayer. The Prophet ﷺ did so at Baṭn Nakhl; the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim] narrated it ﴿وَدَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ تَغْفُلُونَ﴾ when you stand for prayer ﴿عَنْ أَسْلِحَتِكُمْ وَأَمْتِعَتِكُمْ فَيَمِيلُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَيْلَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ by charging at you and seizing you — and this is the reason for the command to take weapons ﴿وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ كَانَ بِكُمْ أَذًى مِنْ مَطَرٍ أَوْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضَى أَنْ تَضَعُوا أَسْلِحَتَكُمْ﴾ so do not carry them. This indicates that carrying them is obligatory when there is no excuse, and it is one of two opinions of al-Shāfiʿī; the second is that it is a Sunna, and this was preferred ﴿وَخُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ﴾ from the enemy, i.e. guard against him as much as you can ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابًا مُهِينًا﴾ possessing humiliation

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمُ الصَّلَوةَ﴾ have finished it ﴿فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ by saying lā ilāha illā Allāh and glorifying ﴿قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَى جُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ lying down, i.e. in every state ﴿فَإِذَا اطْمَأْنَنْتُمْ﴾ you are safe ﴿فَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَوةَ﴾ perform it with its due rights ﴿إِنَّ الصَّلَوةَ كَانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتَابًا﴾ prescribed, i.e. made obligatory ﴿مَوْقُوتًا﴾ i.e. its time is fixed, so it is not delayed beyond it. And [the following] was revealed when he ﷺ sent a group in pursuit of Abū Sufyān and his companions when they returned from Uḥud, and they complained of their wounds

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿وَلَا تَهِنُوا﴾ weaken ﴿فِي ابْتِغَاءِ﴾ pursuit of ﴿الْقَوْمِ﴾ the disbelievers, to fight them ﴿إِنْ تَكُونُوا تَأْلَمُونَ﴾ feel the pain of wounds ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ يَأْلَمُونَ كَمَا تَأْلَمُونَ﴾ i.e. like you, and they do not shrink from fighting you ﴿وَتَرْجُونَ﴾ you ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ of victory and reward for it ﴿مَا لَا يَرْجُونَ﴾ they; so you exceed them in that, and you ought to be more eager for it than they ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا﴾ of everything ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in His making. Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq stole a coat of mail and hid it with a Jew; it was found with him, and Ṭuʿma accused him of it and swore that he had not stolen it. His people asked the Prophet ﷺ to argue on his behalf and clear him, so [the following] was revealed

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) أَنْزَلَ ﴿لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ بِمَا أَرَاكَ﴾ taught you ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ in it ﴿وَلَا تَكُنْ لِلْخَائِنِينَ﴾ such as Ṭuʿma ﴿خَصِيمًا﴾ an advocate disputing on their behalf.

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ﴾ for what you had intended ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿وَلَا تُجَادِلْ عَنِ الَّذِينَ يَخْتَانُونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ betray them by sins, because the ill consequence of their betrayal falls upon them ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَنْ كَانَ خَوَّانًا﴾ much given to betrayal ﴿أَثِيمًا﴾ i.e. He will punish him

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿يَسْتَخْفُونَ﴾ i.e. Ṭuʿma and his people, out of shame ﴿مِنَ النَّاسِ وَلَا يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَهُوَ مَعَهُمْ﴾ by His knowledge ﴿إِذْ يُبَيِّتُونَ﴾ harbour ﴿مَا لَا يَرْضَى مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ of their resolve to swear denying the theft and to accuse the Jew of it ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطًا﴾ in knowledge

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿هَا أَنْتُمْ﴾ O [يَا] ﴿هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ — an address to the people of Ṭuʿma ﴿جَادَلْتُمْ﴾ disputed ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. on behalf of Ṭuʿma and his kin; and it has been read [عَنْهُ] ﴿فِي الْحَيَوةِ الدُّنْيَا فَمَنْ يُجَادِلُ اللَّهَ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾ when He punishes them ﴿أَمْ مَنْ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكِيلًا﴾ who takes charge of their affair and defends them, i.e. no one will do that

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا﴾ a sin by which he harms another, like Ṭuʿma's accusing the Jew ﴿أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ﴾ commits a sin confined to himself ﴿ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ﴾ for it, i.e. repents ﴿يَجِدِ اللَّهَ غَفُورًا﴾ to him ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to him

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَكْسِبْ إِثْمًا﴾ a sin ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَكْسِبُهُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ﴾ because its ill consequence is upon it, and it does not harm another ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا﴾ in His making

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَكْسِبْ خَطِيئَةً﴾ a minor sin ﴿أَوْ إِثْمًا﴾ a major sin ﴿ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ بَرِيئًا﴾ of it ﴿فَقَدِ احْتَمَلَ﴾ has borne ﴿بُهْتَانًا﴾ by his accusing ﴿وَإِثْمًا مُبِينًا﴾ clear, by his committing it

celaleyn:113-113.t: ﴿وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿وَرَحْمَتُهُ﴾ by protection [from error] ﴿لَهَمَّتْ﴾ harboured [the intention] ﴿طَائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ of the people of Ṭuʿma ﴿أَنْ يُضِلُّوكَ﴾ from judging with the truth, by confusing [the matter] for you ﴿وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَضُرُّونَكَ مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ because the ill consequence of their misleading is upon them ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَالْحِكْمَةَ﴾ the rulings in it ﴿وَعَلَّمَكَ مَا لَمْ تَكُنْ تَعْلَمُ﴾ of rulings and the unseen ﴿وَكَانَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ﴾ by that and other things ﴿عَظِيمًا﴾.

celaleyn:114-114.t: ﴿لَا خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِنْ نَجْوَاهُمْ﴾ i.e. of people, i.e. what they converse about privately and talk about ﴿إِلَّا﴾ the private talk of ﴿مَنْ أَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ أَوْ مَعْرُوفٍ﴾ an act of righteousness ﴿أَوْ إِصْلَاحٍ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ﴾ which was mentioned ﴿ابْتِغَاءَ﴾ seeking ﴿مَرْضَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ not anything else of worldly matters ﴿فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ﴾ with nūn and with yāʾ, i.e. Allah ﴿أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾

celaleyn:115-115.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يُشَاقِقِ﴾ opposes ﴿الرَّسُولَ﴾ in the truth he brought ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ الْهُدَى﴾ the truth became manifest to him through the miracles ﴿وَيَتَّبِعْ﴾ a path ﴿غَيْرَ سَبِيلِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ i.e. their path of religion which they are upon, by disbelieving ﴿نُوَلِّهِ مَا تَوَلَّى﴾ We make him an adherent of the misguidance he has turned to, by leaving him and it alone in this world ﴿وَنُصْلِهِ﴾ We enter him in the Hereafter ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ so he burns in it ﴿وَسَاءَتْ مَصِيرًا﴾ a place of return, it is

celaleyn:116-116.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ from the truth

celaleyn:117-117.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ not [مَا] ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ do the idolaters worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ i.e. Allah, i.e. other than Him ﴿إِلَّا إِنَاثًا﴾ feminine idols, such as al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and Manāt ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ not [مَا] ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ do they worship by worshipping them ﴿إِلَّا شَيْطَانًا مَرِيدًا﴾ departing from obedience, because of their obeying him in it — and he is Iblīs

celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ removed him far from His mercy ﴿وَقَالَ﴾ i.e. Satan ﴿لَأَتَّخِذَنَّ﴾ I shall surely make for myself ﴿مِنْ عِبَادِكَ نَصِيبًا﴾ a share ﴿مَفْرُوضًا﴾ allotted, whom I call to obey me

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿وَلَأُضِلَّنَّهُمْ﴾ from the truth by whispering ﴿وَلَأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمْ﴾ I will cast into their hearts [hope of] long life, and that there is no resurrection and no reckoning ﴿وَلَآمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُبَتِّكُنَّ﴾ cut off ﴿آذَانَ الْأَنْعَامِ﴾ and that was done to the baḥīras ﴿وَلَآمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion, by disbelief, making lawful what Allah has forbidden and forbidding what He has made lawful ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَّخِذِ الشَّيْطَانَ وَلِيًّا﴾ taking him as patron and obeying him ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿فَقَدْ خَسِرَ خُسْرَانًا مُبِينًا﴾ clear, because of his destination to the Fire, made everlasting upon him

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿يَعِدُهُمْ﴾ long life ﴿وَيُمَنِّيهِمْ﴾ the attaining of hopes in this world, and that there is no resurrection and no recompense ﴿وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ with that ﴿إِلَّا غُرُورًا﴾ falsehood

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ عَنْهَا مَحِيصًا﴾ a way of escape.

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا﴾ i.e. Allah promised them that, and made it true truly ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. no one ﴿أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ قِيلًا﴾ i.e. in speech. And [the following] was revealed when the Muslims and the People of the Book boasted [to each other]

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿لَيْسَ﴾ the matter dependent ﴿بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ وَلَا أَمَانِيِّ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ﴾ but rather on righteous action ﴿مَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾ either in the Hereafter, or in this world by affliction and trials, as has come in the hadith ﴿وَلَا يَجِدْ لَهُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿وَلِيًّا﴾ who protects him ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرًا﴾ who defends him from it

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ﴾ anything ﴿مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُولَئِكَ يَدْخَلُونَ﴾ in the passive and the active [يَدْخُلُونَ] ﴿الْجَنَّةَ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ نَقِيرًا﴾ the measure of the speck on a date-stone

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. no one ﴿أَحْسَنُ دِينًا مِمَّنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ﴾ i.e. submitted and made his deeds sincere ﴿لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ﴾ affirming [Allah's] oneness ﴿وَاتَّبَعَ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ which accords with the creed of Islam ﴿حَنِيفًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. inclining away from all religions to the upright religion ﴿وَاتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلًا﴾ a chosen one, pure in love for Him

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ as dominion, creation and servants ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُحِيطًا﴾ in knowledge and power, i.e. He has never ceased to be characterised by that

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ﴾ they seek a ruling from you ﴿فِي﴾ the matter of ﴿النِّسَاءِ﴾ and their inheritance ﴿قُلِ﴾ to them ﴿اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran, of the ayah of inheritance, also gives you a ruling ﴿فِي يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ الَّتِي لَا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ مَا كُتِبَ﴾ was made obligatory ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾ of inheritance ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ﴾ O guardians, [averse] to [عَنْ] ﴿أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ because of their unattractiveness, and you prevent them from marrying out of greed for their inheritance; i.e. He gives you a ruling that you are not to do that ﴿وَ﴾ concerning [فِي] ﴿الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ﴾ the young ﴿مِنَ الْوِلْدَانِ﴾ that you give them their rights ﴿وَ﴾ He commands you ﴿أَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتَامَى بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ with justice in inheritance and dower ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِهِ عَلِيمًا﴾ so He will requite you for it.

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ﴾ nominative by a verb which is explained by ﴿خَافَتْ﴾ anticipated ﴿مِنْ بَعْلِهَا﴾ her husband ﴿نُشُوزًا﴾ his haughtiness toward her, by ceasing to share her bed and falling short in her maintenance, out of dislike for her and his eye straying to one more beautiful than her ﴿أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾ turning his face away from her ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يَصَّالَحَا﴾ in it there is assimilation (idghām) of the original tāʾ into the ṣād; and in one reading [يُصْلِحَا], from أَصْلَحَ ﴿بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا﴾ in the division [of nights] and maintenance, by her giving up something to him, seeking that the companionship continue; if she is content with that [so be it]; otherwise the husband must give her her full right or separate from her ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾ than separation, haughtiness and turning away. Allah the Exalted said, explaining what the human being is innately disposed to: ﴿وَأُحْضِرَتِ الْأَنْفُسُ الشُّحَّ﴾ intense avarice, i.e. they are innately disposed to it, as if it were present with them and never absent from them. The meaning is that the woman hardly ever gives up her share of her husband, and the man hardly ever gives himself generously to her when he loves another ﴿وَإِنْ تُحْسِنُوا﴾ in living with women ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ injustice toward them ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ so He will requite you for it

celaleyn:129-129.t: ﴿وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا﴾ make equal ﴿بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ﴾ in love ﴿وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ﴾ on that ﴿فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ﴾ to the one you love in the division [of nights] and maintenance ﴿فَتَذَرُوهَا﴾ i.e. leave the one turned away from ﴿كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ﴾ who is neither unmarried nor has a husband ﴿وَإِنْ تُصْلِحُوا﴾ by justice in the division ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ injustice ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا﴾ of the inclination in your hearts ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to you in that

celaleyn:130-130.t: ﴿وَإِنْ يَتَفَرَّقَا﴾ i.e. the spouses, by divorce ﴿يُغْنِ اللَّهُ كُلًّا﴾ [making each] independent of the other ﴿مِنْ سَعَتِهِ﴾ i.e. His bounty, by providing her with another husband and him with another [wife] ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ وَاسِعًا﴾ in bounty to His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in what He has arranged for them

celaleyn:131-131.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ in the sense of the Books ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ i.e. the Jews and the Christians ﴿وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ O people of the Quran ﴿أَنِ﴾ i.e. بِأَنِ ﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ fear His punishment by obeying Him ﴿وَ﴾ We said to them and to you ﴿إِنْ تَكْفُرُوا﴾ in what you were enjoined with ﴿فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ as creation, dominion and servants, so your disbelief does not harm Him ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَنِيًّا﴾ independent of His creation and their worship ﴿حَمِيدًا﴾ praised in what He does with them

celaleyn:132-132.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ He repeated it for emphasis, to establish what necessitates godfearingness ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا﴾ a witness that what is in them belongs to Him

celaleyn:133-133.t: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ O [يَا] ﴿أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ وَيَأْتِ بِآخَرِينَ﴾ in your place ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ قَدِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:134-134.t: ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ﴾ by his deeds ﴿ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ ثَوَابُ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ for whoever wants it, not with anyone else; so why does one of them seek the baser, and why does he not seek the higher with sincerity toward Him, since what he seeks is found only with Him? ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾.

celaleyn:135-135.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ﴾ standing firm ﴿بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ with justice ﴿شُهَدَاءَ﴾ to the truth ﴿لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ﴾ the testimony be ﴿عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ then testify against them, by acknowledging the truth and not concealing it ﴿أَوْ﴾ against [عَلَى] ﴿الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ إِنْ يَكُنْ﴾ the one testified against ﴿غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا﴾ than you, and knows better their interests ﴿فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى﴾ in your testimony, by favouring the rich to please him, or the poor out of pity for him, so [لِ] ﴿أَنْ﴾ not [لَا] ﴿تَعْدِلُوا﴾ swerve from the truth ﴿وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا﴾ distort the testimony — and in one reading with omission of the first wāw for lightening ﴿أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا﴾ from giving it ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ so He will requite you for it

celaleyn:136-136.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا﴾ persevere in faith ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نُزِّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ, and it is the Quran ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ upon the messengers, in the sense of the Books; and in one reading with the active form in both verbs [نَزَّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ...أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ] ﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ from the truth

celaleyn:137-137.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ in Moses — and they are the Jews ﴿ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا﴾ by worshipping the calf ﴿ثُمَّ آمَنُوا﴾ after it ﴿ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا﴾ in Jesus ﴿ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا﴾ in Muhammad ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ as long as they persist in it ﴿وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ a path to the truth

celaleyn:138-138.t: ﴿بَشِّرْ﴾ inform, O Muhammad ﴿الْمُنَافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful; it is the punishment of the Fire

celaleyn:139-139.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) or naʿt (adjective) of الْمُنَافِقِينَ ﴿يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ because of the strength they imagine in them ﴿أَيَبْتَغُونَ﴾ seek ﴿عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ a question of denial (inkār), i.e. they will not find it with them ﴿فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ in this world and the Hereafter, and none attains it but His friends

celaleyn:140-140.t: ﴿وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ﴾ with the active and the passive form ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran, in Sūrat al-Anʿām ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa), and its noun is omitted, i.e. أَنَّهُ ﴿إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Quran ﴿يُكْفَرُ بِهَا وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers and the mockers ﴿حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا﴾ if you sit with them ﴿مِثْلُهُمْ﴾ in sin ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَامِعُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْكَافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعًا﴾ just as they gathered in this world upon disbelief and mockery.

celaleyn:141-141.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) of the الَّذِينَ before it ﴿يَتَرَبَّصُونَ﴾ wait ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ for misfortunes ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فَتْحٌ﴾ victory and spoils ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ قَالُوا﴾ to you ﴿أَلَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ﴾ in religion and jihad? So give us of the spoils ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ نَصِيبٌ﴾ of victory over you ﴿قَالُوا﴾ to them ﴿أَلَمْ نَسْتَحْوِذْ﴾ gain mastery ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ and were able to capture and kill you, yet we spared you ﴿وَ﴾ did we not [أَلَمْ] ﴿نَمْنَعْكُمْ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ from their prevailing over you, by discouraging them and sending you their news? So we have done you a favour. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿فَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ and them ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ by admitting you into Paradise and them into the Fire ﴿وَلَنْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way to extermination

celaleyn:142-142.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ by displaying the opposite of the disbelief they conceal, so as to ward off its worldly rulings from themselves ﴿وَهُوَ خَادِعُهُمْ﴾ requites them for their deception: they are exposed in this world by Allah's informing His Prophet of what they concealed, and they are punished in the Hereafter ﴿وَإِذَا قَامُوا إِلَى الصَّلَوةِ﴾ with the believers ﴿قَامُوا كُسَالَى﴾ sluggish ﴿يُرَاءُونَ النَّاسَ﴾ with their prayer ﴿وَلَا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ they do not pray ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ for show

celaleyn:143-143.t: ﴿مُذَبْذَبِينَ﴾ wavering ﴿بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ﴾ disbelief and faith ﴿لَا﴾ affiliated ﴿إِلَى هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿وَلَا إِلَى هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ i.e. the believers ﴿وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ﴾ him [هُ] ﴿اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ سَبِيلًا﴾ a path to guidance

celaleyn:144-144.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَتُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ by befriending them ﴿سُلْطَانًا مُبِينًا﴾ a clear proof of your hypocrisy

celaleyn:145-145.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ فِي الدَّرْكِ﴾ the place ﴿الْأَسْفَلِ مِنَ النَّارِ﴾ and it is its bottom ﴿وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُمْ نَصِيرًا﴾ a defender from the punishment

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ﴾ i.e. His punishment, by obeying Him ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾ Ādam ﴿وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾ Ḥawwāʾ (with the long vowel), from one of his left ribs ﴿وَبَثَّ﴾ dispersed and spread ﴿مِنْهُمَا﴾ from Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ ﴿رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً﴾ many ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ﴾ in it the tāʾ of the original form is assimilated (idghām) into the sīn; and in one reading [تَسَاءَلُونَ] it is with the light form, by omitting it, i.e. تَتَسَاءَلُونَ ﴿بِهِ﴾ among yourselves, when one of you says to another: "I ask you by Allah" and "I adjure you by Allah" ﴿وَ﴾ fear ﴿الْأَرْحَامَ﴾ lest you sever them; and in one reading it is in the genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the pronoun in بِهِ, for they used to adjure one another by kinship ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا﴾ guarding your deeds, so He will recompense you for them, i.e. He has always been characterised by that. And the following was revealed concerning an orphan who asked his guardian for his property and he refused him:

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَآتُوا الْيَتَامَى﴾ the young who have no father ﴿أَمْوَالَهُمْ﴾ when they come of age ﴿وَلَا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الْخَبِيثَ﴾ the unlawful ﴿بِالطَّيِّبِ﴾ the lawful, i.e. take it in its place, as you do in taking the good from the orphan's property and putting the bad from your own property in its place ﴿وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ﴾ joined ﴿إِلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. consuming it ﴿كَانَ حُوبًا﴾ a sin ﴿كَبِيرًا﴾ great. When it was revealed they felt constrained about guardianship of orphans, and among them were those who had ten or eight wives and did not deal justly between them, so the following was revealed:

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تُقْسِطُوا﴾ deal justly ﴿فِي الْيَتَامَى﴾ and so felt constrained in their matter, then fear also that you will not deal justly between women when you marry them ﴿فَانْكِحُوا﴾ marry ﴿مَا﴾ in the sense of مَنْ ("whoever") ﴿طَابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ مَثْنَى وَثُلَاثَ وَرُبَاعَ﴾ i.e. two at a time, three at a time and four at a time, and do not exceed that ﴿فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا﴾ among them in maintenance and division [Translator's note: of nights] ﴿فَوَاحِدَةً﴾ marry her ﴿أَوْ﴾ restrict yourselves to ﴿مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ of slave-women, since they do not have the rights that wives have ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. marrying four only, or one, or taking concubines ﴿أَدْنَى﴾ nearer to ﴿أَلَّا تَعُولُوا﴾ act unjustly

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَآتُوا﴾ give ﴿النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ﴾ plural of صَدُقَة: their bridal dowries ﴿نِحْلَةً﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun): a gift given willingly ﴿فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْسًا﴾ a tamyīz (specification) transposed from the fāʿil (agent), i.e. their souls are pleased to give you something of the dowry and so they gift it to you ﴿فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا﴾ wholesome ﴿مَرِيئًا﴾ of praiseworthy outcome, with no harm in it for you in the Hereafter. It was revealed in refutation of those who disliked that

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَلَا تُؤْتُوا﴾ O guardians ﴿السُّفَهَاءَ﴾ the squanderers among men, women and children ﴿أَمْوَالَكُمْ﴾ i.e. their property which is in your hands ﴿الَّتِي جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ قِيَامًا﴾ a maṣdar of قَامَ, i.e. it sustains your livelihood and sets right your crookedness, for they would put it in the wrong place; and in one reading [قِيَمًا], plural of قِيمَة: that by which goods are valued ﴿وَارْزُقُوهُمْ فِيهَا﴾ feed them from it ﴿وَاكْسُوهُمْ وَقُولُوا لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا﴾ give them a fair promise that you will give them their property when they become mature

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَابْتَلُوا﴾ test ﴿الْيَتَامَى﴾ before puberty, in their religion and in their handling of their affairs ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغُوا النِّكَاحَ﴾ i.e. become fit for it, through wet dreams or age, which is the completion of fifteen years according to al-Shāfiʿī ﴿فَإِنْ آنَسْتُمْ﴾ you perceive ﴿مِنْهُمْ رُشْدًا﴾ soundness in their religion and their property ﴿فَادْفَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوهَا﴾ O guardians ﴿إِسْرَافًا﴾ without right; a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿وَبِدَارًا﴾ i.e. hastening to spend it, for fear ﴿أَنْ يَكْبَرُوا﴾ mature, and you would then be obliged to hand it over to them ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ﴾ of the guardians ﴿غَنِيًّا فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ﴾ i.e. abstain from the orphan's property and refrain from consuming it ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ فَقِيرًا فَلْيَأْكُلْ﴾ of it ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ to the extent of the wage for his work ﴿فَإِذَا دَفَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. to the orphans ﴿أَمْوَالَهُمْ فَأَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ that they have received it and you are cleared, lest a dispute arise and you have recourse to evidence; and this command is guidance (irshād) ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ﴾ the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) ﴿حَسِيبًا﴾ guarding the deeds of His creation and taking them to account

celaleyn:7-7.t: And the following was revealed in refutation of the practice of the Jāhiliyya of not giving women and young children inheritance: ﴿لِلرِّجَالِ﴾ the children and relatives ﴿نَصِيبٌ﴾ a share ﴿مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوَالِدَانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ﴾ who have died ﴿وَلِلنِّسَاءِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوَالِدَانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ مِمَّا قَلَّ مِنْهُ﴾ i.e. of the wealth ﴿أَوْ كَثُرَ﴾ Allah has made it ﴿نَصِيبًا مَفْرُوضًا﴾ definitively due to be handed over to them

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَإِذَا حَضَرَ الْقِسْمَةَ﴾ of the inheritance ﴿أُولُوا الْقُرْبَى﴾ relatives who do not inherit ﴿وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينُ فَارْزُقُوهُمْ مِنْهُ﴾ something, before the division ﴿وَقُولُوا﴾ O guardians ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ if the heirs are minors ﴿قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا﴾ kind, by apologising to them that you do not own it and that it belongs to the minors. Of this it has been said that it is abrogated, and it has been said: no, but people have been lax in neglecting it; on this view it is recommended (nadb). And from Ibn ʿAbbās: it is obligatory

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَلْيَخْشَ﴾ i.e. let them fear for the orphans ﴿الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا﴾ i.e. were near to leaving ﴿مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾ i.e. after their death ﴿ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافًا﴾ young children ﴿خَافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ loss ﴿فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ in the matter of the orphans, and let them do to them what they would like to be done to their own offspring after them ﴿وَلْيَقُولُوا﴾ to the dying person ﴿قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا﴾ right, by telling him to give in charity less than his third and leave the rest to his heirs, and not leave them dependent on others

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَالَ الْيَتَامَى ظُلْمًا﴾ without right ﴿إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ﴾ i.e. their fill ﴿نَارًا﴾ because it leads to it ﴿وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ﴾ in the active and the passive: they will enter ﴿سَعِيرًا﴾ an intense fire in which they burn

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ﴾ commands you ﴿اللَّهُ فِي﴾ the matter of ﴿أَوْلَادِكُمْ﴾ with what is mentioned: ﴿لِلذَّكَرِ﴾ among them ﴿مِثْلُ حَظِّ﴾ the share of ﴿الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾ when two are together with him, so he has half the wealth and they have half; if there is one with him, she has a third and he has two thirds; and if he is alone, he takes all the wealth ﴿فَإِنْ كُنَّ﴾ i.e. the children ﴿نِسَاءً﴾ only ﴿فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَ﴾ the deceased; and likewise two, because it belongs to two sisters by His saying {فَلَهُمَا الثُّلُثَانِ مِمَّا تَرَكَ} ("then they have two thirds of what he left"), so they [Translator's note: the two daughters] have more right; and because a daughter is entitled to a third along with a male, so with a female she is even more entitled. As for {وَفَوْقَ}, it has been said that it is a connective (ṣila) [Translator's note: i.e. redundant], and it has been said that it is to prevent the supposition that the share increases with the increase in number, since the entitlement of two daughters to two thirds is understood from assigning a third to the one with a male ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَتْ﴾ the daughter ﴿وَاحِدَةً﴾ and in one reading in the nominative, so كَانَ is complete (tāmma) ﴿فَلَهَا النِّصْفُ وَلِأَبَوَيْهِ﴾ i.e. of the deceased; and substituted (badal) from them is ﴿لِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ﴾ male or female. The subtle point of the badal is to convey that they do not share in it [Translator's note: i.e. each has a full sixth]. The son's child is assimilated to the child, and the grandfather to the father ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَوَرِثَهُ أَبَوَاهُ﴾ alone or with a spouse ﴿فَلِأُمِّهِ﴾ with ḍamma and kasra on the hamza, [Translator's note: the latter] to avoid passing from a ḍamma to a kasra because of its heaviness, in both places ﴿الثُّلُثُ﴾ i.e. a third of the wealth, or of what remains after the spouse, and the rest is for the father ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ﴾ i.e. two or more, male or female ﴿فَلِأُمِّهِ السُّدُسُ﴾ and the rest is for the father, and nothing for the siblings. And the inheritance of those mentioned, of what is mentioned, is ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ executing ﴿وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي﴾ in the active and the passive ﴿بِهَا أَوْ﴾ paying ﴿دَيْنٍ﴾ owed by him. The bequest is placed before the debt, though it comes after it in settlement, to give it importance ﴿آبَاؤُكُمْ وَأَبْنَاؤُكُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿لَا تَدْرُونَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ لَكُمْ نَفْعًا﴾ in this world and the Hereafter: one thinks his son is more beneficial to him and gives him the inheritance, and the father turns out more beneficial, and vice versa. Only Allah knows that, so He has prescribed the inheritance for you ﴿فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in what He has arranged for them, i.e. He has always been characterised by that

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَلَكُمْ نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ أَزْوَاجُكُمْ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ﴾ by you or by others ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ فَلَكُمُ الرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْنَ مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِينَ بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ﴾ and the son's child is assimilated to the child in this by consensus (ijmāʿ) ﴿وَلَهُنَّ﴾ i.e. the wives, whether several or not ﴿الرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَإِنْ كَانَ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ﴾ by them or by others ﴿فَلَهُنَّ الثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ تُوصُونَ بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ﴾ and the son's child in this is like the child, by consensus ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa), and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿كَلَالَةً﴾ i.e. he has neither parent nor child ﴿أَوِ امْرَأَةٌ﴾ inherited from as kalāla ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ i.e. the one inherited from as kalāla ﴿أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ﴾ i.e. from the mother, and Ibn Masʿūd and others read it so ﴿فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ﴾ of what he left ﴿فَإِنْ كَانُوا﴾ i.e. the brothers and sisters from the mother ﴿أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. than one ﴿فَهُمْ شُرَكَاءُ فِي الثُّلُثِ﴾ their males and females being equal in it ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصَى بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَارٍّ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of يُوصَى, i.e. not bringing harm upon the heirs by bequeathing more than a third ﴿وَصِيَّةً﴾ an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun) for يُوصِيكُمْ ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of the shares He has arranged for His creation ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾ in deferring punishment from those who oppose Him. The Sunna has restricted the inheritance of those mentioned to those in whom there is no impediment such as killing, difference of religion or slavery

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ rulings mentioned, concerning the orphans and what follows ﴿حُدُودُ اللَّهِ﴾ His laws which He has set for His servants to act upon and not transgress ﴿وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ in what He has ruled ﴿يُدْخِلْهُ﴾ with yāʾ and with nūn, as a shift (iltifāt) ﴿جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ﴾ in both ways ﴿نَارًا خَالِدًا فِيهَا وَلَهُ﴾ in it ﴿عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ﴾ involving humiliation. In the pronouns in the two ayahs the wording of مَنْ is taken into account, and in خَالِدِينَ its meaning.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَالَّتِي يَأْتِينَ الْفَاحِشَةَ﴾ fornication ﴿مِنْ نِسَائِكُمْ فَاسْتَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ أَرْبَعَةً مِنْكُمْ﴾ i.e. from among your Muslim men ﴿فَإِنْ شَهِدُوا﴾ against them of it ﴿فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾ confine them ﴿فِي الْبُيُوتِ﴾ and prevent them from mixing with people ﴿حَتَّى يَتَوَفَّاهُنَّ الْمَوْتُ﴾ i.e. its angels ﴿أَوْ﴾ until ﴿أَنْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way out of it. They were commanded this at the beginning of Islam; then a way was made for them: flogging the unmarried woman a hundred [Translator's note: lashes] and exiling her for a year, and stoning the muḥṣana (married woman). And in the hadith, when he explained the ḥadd punishment, he said: "Take from me, take from me: Allah has made a way for them." Narrated by Muslim. [Translator's note: the source text writes the Quranic word as وَالَّتِي; the muṣḥaf reads وَاللَّاتِي.]

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَالَّذَانِ﴾ with the nūn light and doubled ﴿يَأْتِيَانِهَا﴾ i.e. the lewdness, fornication or sodomy ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ i.e. of the men ﴿فَآذُوهُمَا﴾ by insult and beating with sandals ﴿فَإِنْ تَابَا﴾ from it ﴿وَأَصْلَحَا﴾ their conduct ﴿فَأَعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمَا﴾ and do not harm them ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ تَوَّابًا﴾ towards whoever repents ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to him. This is abrogated by the ḥadd if fornication is meant by it, and likewise if sodomy is meant by it according to al-Shāfiʿī; but according to him the passive partner is not stoned even if muḥṣan, rather he is flogged and exiled. That sodomy is meant is more apparent, as evidenced by the dual pronoun; and the one who held the first view said that the fornicator and the fornicatress are meant, but this is refuted by their being specified by مِنْ attached to the pronoun of the men, and by their sharing in the harm, the repentance and the turning away, which is specific to men, given the confinement mentioned before for women

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا التَّوْبَةُ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. that which He has by His bounty written upon Himself to accept ﴿لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السُّوءَ﴾ disobedience ﴿بِجَهَالَةٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. being ignorant when they disobeyed their Lord ﴿ثُمَّ يَتُوبُونَ مِنْ﴾ a time ﴿قَرِيبٍ﴾ before the death-rattle ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ يَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ accepts their repentance ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in His dealing with them

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَلَيْسَتِ التَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ﴾ sins ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ﴾ and he begins the throes of death ﴿قَالَ﴾ upon seeing what he is in ﴿إِنِّي تُبْتُ الْآنَ﴾ so that does not benefit him and is not accepted from him ﴿وَلَا الَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ﴾ if they repent in the Hereafter upon seeing the punishment, it is not accepted from them ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَعْتَدْنَا﴾ We have prepared ﴿لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful

celaleyn:146-146.t: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا﴾ from hypocrisy ﴿وَأَصْلَحُوا﴾ their deeds ﴿وَاعْتَصَمُوا﴾ trusted ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَأَخْلَصُوا دِينَهُمْ لِلَّهِ﴾ from showing off ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in what they are given ﴿وَسَوْفَ يُؤْتِ اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ in the Hereafter; it is Paradise

celaleyn:147-147.t: ﴿مَا يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ بِعَذَابِكُمْ إِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ﴾ His blessings ﴿وَآمَنْتُمْ﴾ in Him; the question has the sense of negation, i.e. He will not punish you ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ شَاكِرًا﴾ of the deeds of the believers, by rewarding [them] ﴿عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation.

celaleyn:148-148.t: ﴿لَا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ الْجَهْرَ بِالسُّوءِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ from anyone, i.e. He punishes him for it ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ ظُلِمَ﴾ for He does not take him to task for saying it openly, by telling of the wrong of the one who wronged him and supplicating against him ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعًا﴾ of what is said ﴿عَلِيمًا﴾ of what is done

celaleyn:149-149.t: ﴿إِنْ تُبْدُوا﴾ display ﴿خَيْرًا﴾ of righteous deeds ﴿أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ﴾ do it secretly ﴿أَوْ تَعْفُوا عَنْ سُوءٍ﴾ a wrong ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا قَدِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:150-150.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُفَرِّقُوا بَيْنَ اللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ﴾ by believing in Him but not in them ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ نُؤْمِنُ بِبَعْضٍ﴾ of the messengers ﴿وَنَكْفُرُ بِبَعْضٍ﴾ of them ﴿وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ﴾ disbelief and faith ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾ a path which they take

celaleyn:151-151.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ حَقًّا﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising the content of the clause before it ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابًا مُهِينًا﴾ possessing humiliation; it is the punishment of the Fire

celaleyn:152-152.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ﴾ all of them ﴿وَلَمْ يُفَرِّقُوا بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ أُولَئِكَ سَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِمْ﴾ with nūn and with yāʾ [يُؤْتِيهِمْ] ﴿أُجُورَهُمْ﴾ the reward of their deeds ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا﴾ to His friends ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to the people of obedience to Him

celaleyn:153-153.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Jews ﴿أَنْ تُنَزِّلَ [أَنْ تَنَزَّلَ] عَلَيْهِمْ كِتَابًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾ all at once, as it was sent down upon Moses — out of obstinacy; so if you find that grave ﴿فَقَدْ سَأَلُوا﴾ i.e. their forefathers ﴿مُوسَى أَكْبَرَ﴾ greater ﴿مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالُوا أَرِنَا اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً﴾ visibly ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ﴾ death, as a punishment for them ﴿بِظُلْمِهِمْ﴾ in that they were obstinate in asking ﴿ثُمَّ اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ﴾ as a god ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾ the miracles [testifying] to the oneness of Allah ﴿فَعَفَوْنَا عَنْ ذَلِكَ﴾ and did not exterminate them ﴿وَآتَيْنَا مُوسَى سُلْطَانًا مُبِينًا﴾ clear, manifest authority over them, in that he commanded them to kill themselves as repentance, and they obeyed him

celaleyn:154-154.t: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَهُمُ الطُّورَ﴾ the mountain ﴿بِمِيثَاقِهِمْ﴾ because of taking the covenant from them, so that they would fear, and they accepted it ﴿وَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ﴾ while it was overshadowing them ﴿ادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ﴾ the gate of the town ﴿سُجَّدًا﴾ a prostration of bowing ﴿وَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ لَا تَعْدُوا﴾ — and in one reading with fatḥa on the ʿayn and doubling of the dāl, in which there is assimilation (idghām) of the original tāʾ into the dāl, i.e. لَا تَعْتَدُوا ﴿فِي السَّبْتِ﴾ by catching fish on it ﴿وَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُمْ مِيثَاقًا غَلِيظًا﴾ on that, but they broke it.

celaleyn:155-155.t: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ﴾ مَا is redundant (zāʾida), and the bāʾ is causal, attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, i.e. "We cursed them because of their breaking" ﴿مِيثَاقَهُمْ وَكُفْرِهِمْ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَقَتْلِهِمُ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَقَوْلِهِمْ﴾ to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ﴾ they do not take in your words ﴿بَلْ طَبَعَ﴾ sealed ﴿اللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ so they do not take in admonition ﴿فَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ of them, like ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and his companions

celaleyn:156-156.t: ﴿وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ a second time, in Jesus; the bāʾ is repeated to separate between it and what it is conjoined to ﴿وَقَوْلِهِمْ عَلَى مَرْيَمَ بُهْتَانًا عَظِيمًا﴾ in that they accused her of fornication

celaleyn:157-157.t: ﴿وَقَوْلِهِمْ﴾ boastfully ﴿إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا الْمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ﴾ as they claimed; i.e. for the sum of that We punished them. Allah the Exalted said, giving them the lie about killing him: ﴿وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَكِنْ شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ﴾ the one killed and crucified — who was their companion — was made to resemble Jesus, i.e. Allah cast his likeness upon him, so they thought he was him ﴿وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ﴾ i.e. about Jesus ﴿لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ﴾ about his killing, since some of them said, when they saw the one killed: "The face is the face of Jesus, but the body is not his body, so it is not him," while others said: "Rather, it is he" ﴿مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ﴾ of his killing ﴿مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا اتِّبَاعَ الظَّنِّ﴾ a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), i.e. but they follow in it the conjecture they imagined ﴿وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًا﴾ an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida, emphasising circumstantial) for the negation of the killing

celaleyn:158-158.t: ﴿بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا﴾ in His dominion ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in His making

celaleyn:159-159.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ not [مَا] ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ﴾ anyone ﴿إِلَّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ﴾ in Jesus ﴿قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ﴾ i.e. [the death of] the one of the People of the Book, when he sees the angels of death, so his faith will not benefit him; or before the death of Jesus, when he descends near the Hour, as has come in a hadith ﴿وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ يَكُونُ﴾ Jesus ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًا﴾ to what they did when he was sent to them

celaleyn:160-160.t: ﴿فَبِظُلْمٍ﴾ i.e. because of wrongdoing ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا﴾ they are the Jews ﴿حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّبَاتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ﴾ they are those in His saying, Exalted is He: {حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ} — the ayah ﴿وَبِصَدِّهِمْ﴾ people ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion, a hindering ﴿كَثِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:161-161.t: ﴿وَأَخْذِهِمُ الرِّبَا وَقَدْ نُهُوا عَنْهُ﴾ in the Torah ﴿وَأَكْلِهِمْ أَمْوَالَ النَّاسِ بِالْبَاطِلِ﴾ through bribes in judgement ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ مِنْهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful

celaleyn:162-162.t: ﴿لَكِنِ الرَّاسِخُونَ﴾ the firmly established ﴿فِي الْعِلْمِ مِنْهُمْ﴾ like ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām ﴿وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ the Emigrants and the Helpers ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ of the Books ﴿وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلَوةَ﴾ accusative as praise (naṣb ʿalā al-madḥ), and it has been read in the nominative ﴿وَالْمُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَوةَ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ أُولَئِكَ سَنُؤْتِيهِمْ﴾ with nūn and with yāʾ ﴿أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ it is Paradise.

celaleyn:163-163.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ كَمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى نُوحٍ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ ﴿وَ﴾ as [كَمَا] ﴿أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ﴾ his two sons ﴿وَيَعْقُوبَ﴾ son of Isaac ﴿وَالْأَسْبَاطِ﴾ his children ﴿وَعِيسَى وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهَارُونَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ وَآتَيْنَا﴾ his father ﴿دَاوُدَ زَبُورًا﴾ with fatḥa, a name for the Book given; and with ḍamma, a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of مَزْبُورًا, i.e. written

celaleyn:164-164.t: ﴿وَ﴾ We sent ﴿رُسُلًا قَدْ قَصَصْنَاهُمْ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَرُسُلًا لَمْ نَقْصُصْهُمْ عَلَيْكَ﴾ It is narrated that He, Exalted is He, sent eight thousand prophets: four thousand from the Children of Israel and four thousand from the rest of mankind; the Shaykh said this in Sūrat Ghāfir ﴿وَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ مُوسَى﴾ without intermediary ﴿تَكْلِيمًا﴾

celaleyn:165-165.t: ﴿رُسُلًا﴾ a badal (substitute) of the رُسُلًا before it ﴿مُبَشِّرِينَ﴾ of reward to whoever believes ﴿وَمُنْذِرِينَ﴾ of punishment to whoever disbelieves.
