We sent them ﴿لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى اللَّهِ حُجَّةٌ﴾ to be put forward ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ the sending of ﴿الرُّسُلِ﴾ to them, so that they would say: {رَبَّنَا لَوْلَا أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ آيَاتِكَ وَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ}; so We sent them to cut off their excuse ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا﴾ in His dominion ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in His making. And [the following] was revealed when the Jews were asked about his ﷺ prophethood and denied it

celaleyn:166-166.t: ﴿لَكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ﴾ makes clear your prophethood ﴿بِمَا أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ of the inimitable Quran ﴿أَنْزَلَهُ﴾ bound up ﴿بِعِلْمِهِ﴾ i.e. knowing it, or with His knowledge in it ﴿وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ يَشْهَدُونَ﴾ for you as well ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا﴾ to that

celaleyn:167-167.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ in Allah ﴿وَصَدُّوا﴾ people ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ the religion of Islam, by concealing the description of Muhammad ﷺ — and they are the Jews ﴿قَدْ ضَلُّوا ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ from the truth

celaleyn:168-168.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ in Allah ﴿وَظَلَمُوا﴾ His Prophet, by concealing his description ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ طَرِيقًا﴾ of the paths

celaleyn:169-169.t: ﴿إِلَّا طَرِيقَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ i.e. the path leading to it ﴿خَالِدِينَ﴾ destined for eternity ﴿فِيهَا﴾ when they enter it ﴿أَبَدًا وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا﴾ easy

celaleyn:170-170.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ i.e. people of Mecca ﴿قَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الرَّسُولُ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ ﴿بِالْحَقِّ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَآمِنُوا﴾ in him, and aim for ﴿خَيْرًا لَكُمْ﴾ than what you are in ﴿وَإِنْ تَكْفُرُوا﴾ in him ﴿فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ as dominion, creation and servants, so your disbelief does not harm Him ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in what He does with them

celaleyn:171-171.t: ﴿يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Gospel ﴿لَا تَغْلُوا﴾ go beyond the bound ﴿فِي دِينِكُمْ وَلَا تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا﴾ the saying that is ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ of declaring Him free of partner and child ﴿إِنَّمَا الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُ أَلْقَاهَا﴾ Allah conveyed it ﴿إِلَى مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌ﴾ i.e. possessing a spirit ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ it is attributed to Him, Exalted is He, to honour him; and he is not, as you claimed, the son of Allah, or a god with Him, or the third of three, because the possessor of a spirit is composite, and God is free of compositeness and of having the composite attributed to Him ﴿فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَلَا تَقُولُوا﴾ the gods are ﴿ثَلَاثَةٌ﴾ Allah, Jesus and his mother ﴿انْتَهُوا﴾ from that, and bring ﴿خَيْرًا لَكُمْ﴾ than it — and it is the affirmation of [Allah's] oneness ﴿إِنَّمَا اللَّهُ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ declaring Him free of [عَنْ] ﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ as creation, dominion and servants, and being owned is incompatible with sonship ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا﴾ a witness to that

celaleyn:172-172.t: ﴿لَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفَ﴾ be too proud and disdainful ﴿الْمَسِيحُ﴾ whom you claimed to be a god, [too proud] to [عَنْ] ﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ عَبْدًا لِلَّهِ وَلَا الْمَلَائِكَةُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ﴾ to Allah are too proud to be servants. This is one of the finest digressions (istiṭrād); it was mentioned to refute whoever claimed that they are gods or daughters of Allah, just as what precedes it refuted the Christians who claimed that, whom it is intended to address ﴿وَمَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفْ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَيَسْتَكْبِرْ فَسَيَحْشُرُهُمْ إِلَيْهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ in the Hereafter

celaleyn:173-173.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ﴾ the reward of their deeds ﴿وَيَزِيدُهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never occurred to the heart of a human being ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اسْتَنْكَفُوا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ from worshipping Him ﴿فَيُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful; it is the punishment of the Fire ﴿وَلَا يَجِدُونَ لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿وَلِيًّا﴾ who wards it off from them ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرًا﴾ who protects them from it

celaleyn:174-174.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بُرْهَانٌ﴾ a proof ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ against you, and it is the Prophet ﷺ ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ نُورًا مُبِينًا﴾ clear, and it is the Quran

celaleyn:175-175.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَاعْتَصَمُوا بِهِ فَسَيُدْخِلُهُمْ فِي رَحْمَةٍ مِنْهُ وَفَضْلٍ وَيَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَيْهِ صِرَاطًا﴾ a path ﴿مُسْتَقِيمًا﴾ it is the religion of Islam

celaleyn:176-176.t: ﴿يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ﴾ about kalāla ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِي الْكَلَالَةِ إِنِ امْرُؤٌ﴾ nominative by a verb which is explained by ﴿هَلَكَ﴾ died ﴿لَيْسَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ﴾ i.e. nor parent — and this is kalāla ﴿وَلَهُ أُخْتٌ﴾ of both parents or of the father ﴿فَلَهَا نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ وَهُوَ﴾ i.e. the brother, likewise ﴿يَرِثُهَا﴾ all that she left ﴿إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهَا وَلَدٌ﴾ but if she has a male child, he gets nothing; or a female, then he gets what remains of her share. And if the sister or the brother is from the mother, then his fixed share is a sixth, as preceded at the beginning of the sūra ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَتَا﴾ i.e. the sisters ﴿اثْنَتَيْنِ﴾ i.e. or more, because it was revealed about Jābir, who died leaving sisters ﴿فَلَهُمَا الثُّلُثَانِ مِمَّا تَرَكَ﴾ the brother ﴿وَإِنْ كَانُوا﴾ i.e. the heirs ﴿إِخْوَةً رِجَالًا وَنِسَاءً فَلِلذَّكَرِ﴾ of them ﴿مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾ the laws of your religion, so [لِ] ﴿أَنْ﴾ not [لَا] ﴿تَضِلُّوا وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ including inheritance. The two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim] narrated from al-Barāʾ that it was the last ayah revealed, i.e. of [those on] the shares of inheritance. [Translator's note: Jābir was alive when the ayah was revealed — he was ill and had only sisters; the text's "who died" (وَقَدْ مَاتَ) is translated as written.]

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَرِثُوا النِّسَاءَ﴾ i.e. their persons ﴿كَرْهًا﴾ with fatḥa and ḍamma, two dialectal forms, i.e. compelling them to that. In the Jāhiliyya they used to inherit the wives of their relatives: if they wished they married them without a dowry, or married her off and took her dowry, or prevented her [Translator's note: from marrying] until she ransomed herself with what she had inherited or died and they inherited from her. So they were forbidden that ﴿وَلَا﴾ that ﴿تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ﴾ i.e. prevent your wives from marrying others by keeping them, while you have no desire for them, to harm them ﴿لِتَذْهَبُوا بِبَعْضِ مَا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ of the dowry ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ مُبَيَّنَةٍ﴾ with fatḥa and kasra on the yāʾ [مُبَيِّنَةٍ], i.e. made clear, or it is clear: i.e. fornication or recalcitrance (nushūz); then you may put pressure on them until they ransom themselves from you and seek khulʿ (divorce for compensation) ﴿وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ i.e. with graciousness in speech, maintenance and spending the night ﴿فَإِنْ كَرِهْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ then be patient ﴿فَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا﴾ and perhaps He will put that in them, by granting you a righteous child from them

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمُ اسْتِبْدَالَ زَوْجٍ مَكَانَ زَوْجٍ﴾ i.e. taking her in her place, by your having divorced her ﴿وَ﴾ having (qad) ﴿آتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ﴾ i.e. the wives ﴿قِنْطَارًا﴾ much wealth as dowry ﴿فَلَا تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئًا أَتَأْخُذُونَهُ بُهْتَانًا﴾ wrongfully ﴿وَإِثْمًا مُبِينًا﴾ clear. Their accusative is as ḥāl (circumstantial), and the interrogative is for rebuke and for denial

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ﴾ i.e. on what grounds ﴿وَقَدْ أَفْضَى﴾ has reached ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ﴾ through intercourse, which establishes the dowry ﴿وَأَخَذْنَ مِنْكُمْ مِيثَاقًا﴾ a covenant ﴿غَلِيظًا﴾ firm, which is what Allah has commanded: retaining them in kindness or releasing them with excellence

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَلَا تَنْكِحُوا مَا﴾ in the sense of مَنْ ("whom") ﴿نَكَحَ آبَاؤُكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾ of your doing that, for it is pardoned ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. marrying them ﴿كَانَ فَاحِشَةً﴾ vile ﴿وَمَقْتًا﴾ a cause of loathing from Allah, which is the most intense hatred ﴿وَسَاءَ﴾ evil is ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾ as a way, that

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ﴾ to marry them; and it includes grandmothers on the father's or mother's side ﴿وَبَنَاتُكُمْ﴾ and it includes the daughters of children, however far down ﴿وَأَخَوَاتُكُمْ﴾ on the father's or mother's side ﴿وَعَمَّاتُكُمْ﴾ i.e. the sisters of your fathers and grandfathers ﴿وَخَالَاتُكُمْ﴾ i.e. the sisters of your mothers and grandmothers ﴿وَبَنَاتُ الْأَخِ وَبَنَاتُ الْأُخْتِ﴾ and their children are included in them ﴿وَأُمَّهَاتُكُمُ الَّتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ﴾ before the completion of two years, five sucklings, as the hadith has made clear ﴿وَأَخَوَاتُكُمْ مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ﴾ and attached to that by the Sunna are the daughters through it, namely those whom the women he has had intercourse with suckled, and the paternal aunts, maternal aunts, brothers' daughters and sisters' daughters through it, because of the hadith: "Suckling makes unlawful what lineage makes unlawful." Narrated by al-Bukhārī and Muslim. ﴿وَأُمَّهَاتُ نِسَائِكُمْ وَرَبَائِبُكُمُ﴾ plural of رَبِيبَة, which is the wife's daughter by another man ﴿الَّتِي فِي حُجُورِكُمْ﴾ whom you raise; an adjective (ṣifa) in accord with what is usual, so it has no contrary implication (mafhūm) ﴿مِنْ نِسَائِكُمُ الَّتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ﴾ i.e. with whom you have had intercourse ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ in marrying their daughters if you have separated from them ﴿وَحَلَائِلُ﴾ the wives of ﴿أَبْنَائِكُمُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ أَصْلَابِكُمْ﴾ unlike those you have adopted, whose wives you may marry ﴿وَأَنْ تَجْمَعُوا بَيْنَ الْأُخْتَيْنِ﴾ by lineage or suckling, in marriage; and attached to these by the Sunna is combining a woman with her paternal or maternal aunt. It is permitted to marry each one separately, and to own both together and have intercourse with one ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾ in the Jāhiliyya, of their marrying some of those mentioned; there is no blame on you for it ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا﴾ for what you did before the prohibition ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to you in that.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَ﴾ forbidden to you are ﴿الْمُحْصَنَاتُ﴾ i.e. those who have husbands ﴿مِنَ النِّسَاءِ﴾ to marry them before they separate from their husbands, whether they are free Muslim women or not ﴿إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ of slave-women through capture: you may have intercourse with them, even if they have husbands in the abode of war, after establishing that the womb is free (istibrāʾ) ﴿كِتَابَ اللَّهِ﴾ accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. He has prescribed that ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَحَلَّ﴾ in the active and the passive [وَأُحِلَّ] ﴿لَكُمْ مَا وَرَاءَ ذَلِكُمْ﴾ i.e. other than the women forbidden to you ﴿أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا﴾ seek women ﴿بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ﴾ by dowry or price ﴿مُحْصِنِينَ﴾ marrying ﴿غَيْرَ مُسَافِحِينَ﴾ fornicating ﴿فَمَا﴾ whomever ﴿اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ﴾ enjoyed ﴿بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ﴾ of those you have married, through intercourse ﴿فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ their dowries which you assigned them ﴿فَرِيضَةً وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا تَرَاضَيْتُمْ﴾ you and they ﴿بِهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْفَرِيضَةِ﴾ of remitting it or part of it, or adding to it ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in what He has arranged for them

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنْكُمْ طَوْلًا﴾ i.e. means for ﴿أَنْ يَنْكِحَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ﴾ the free women ﴿الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾ this follows what is usual, so it has no contrary implication (mafhūm) ﴿فَمِنْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ let him marry ﴿مِنْ فَتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ﴾ so be content with its outward [Translator's note: form] and leave the inner secrets to Him, for He knows their details; and many a slave-woman surpasses the free woman in it. This is to make marrying slave-women feel acceptable ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ i.e. you and they are equal in religion, so do not disdain marrying them ﴿فَانْكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ﴾ their masters ﴿وَآتُوهُنَّ﴾ give them ﴿أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ their dowries ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ without delay or reduction ﴿مُحْصَنَاتٍ﴾ chaste; a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ﴾ fornicating openly ﴿وَلَا مُتَّخِذَاتِ أَخْدَانٍ﴾ lovers who fornicate with them secretly ﴿فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ﴾ are given in marriage, and in one reading in the active: they marry ﴿فَإِنْ أَتَيْنَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ﴾ fornication ﴿فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى الْمُحْصَنَاتِ﴾ the free virgins, if they fornicate ﴿مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ the ḥadd: so they are flogged fifty [Translator's note: lashes] and exiled for half a year, and male slaves are judged by analogy with them. Iḥṣān (married status) is not made a condition for the ḥadd being due, but rather to convey that there is no stoning for them at all ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. marrying slave-women when lacking means ﴿لِمَنْ خَشِيَ﴾ fears ﴿الْعَنَتَ﴾ fornication; its root meaning is hardship, and fornication is called by it because it is the cause of it, through the ḥadd in this world and punishment in the Hereafter ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ unlike the free man who does not fear it: it is not lawful for him to marry her; and likewise whoever has the means for a free woman; and this is the view of al-Shāfiʿī. Excluded by His saying {مِنْ فَتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ} are the disbelieving women: it is not lawful for him to marry her even if he lacks means and fears ﴿وَأَنْ تَصْبِرُوا﴾ from marrying slave-women ﴿خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ lest the child become a slave ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ by granting latitude in that

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ﴾ the laws of your religion and the interests of your affairs ﴿وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ سُنَنَ﴾ the ways of ﴿الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ of the prophets, in making lawful and unlawful, so that you follow them ﴿وَيَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ bring you back from the disobedience to Him which you were in to obedience to Him ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of you ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in what He has arranged for you.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ He repeated it in order to build upon it ﴿وَيُرِيدُ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الشَّهَوَاتِ﴾ the Jews and the Christians, or the Magians, or the fornicators ﴿أَنْ تَمِيلُوا مَيْلًا عَظِيمًا﴾ turn away from the truth by committing what is forbidden to you, so that you become like them

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُخَفِّفَ عَنْكُمْ﴾ make the rulings of the Sharia easy for you ﴿وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ ضَعِيفًا﴾ unable to keep away from women and desires

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْبَاطِلِ﴾ by what is unlawful in the Sharia, such as usury and usurpation ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿أَنْ تَكُونَ﴾ occur ﴿تِجَارَةٌ﴾ and in one reading in the accusative [تِجَارَةً], i.e. the wealth is the wealth of trade, issuing ﴿عَنْ تَرَاضٍ مِنْكُمْ﴾ and with willingness, then you may consume it ﴿وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ by committing what leads to their destruction, whatever it may be, in this world or the Hereafter, as indicated by ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا﴾ in His forbidding you that

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. what is forbidden ﴿عُدْوَانًا﴾ overstepping the lawful; a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿وَظُلْمًا﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ﴾ We will make him enter ﴿نَارًا﴾ in which he burns ﴿وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا﴾ easy

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبَائِرَ مَا تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ﴾ and they are those for which a threat has come, such as killing, fornication and theft; and from Ibn ʿAbbās: they are nearer to seven hundred ﴿نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ﴾ the minor sins, through acts of obedience ﴿وَنُدْخِلْكُمْ مُدْخَلًا﴾ with ḍamma and fatḥa on the mīm, i.e. an entering or a place ﴿كَرِيمًا﴾ which is the Garden

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَلَا تَتَمَنَّوْا مَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ﴾ in respect of this world or religion, lest it lead to mutual envy and hatred ﴿لِلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبٌ﴾ reward ﴿مِمَّا اكْتَسَبُوا﴾ because of what they did of jihad and other things ﴿وَلِلنِّسَاءِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا اكْتَسَبْنَ﴾ of obeying their husbands and guarding their chastity. It was revealed when Umm Salama said: "Would that we were men, so that we could fight in jihad and have the like of the men's reward." ﴿وَاسْأَلُوا﴾ with hamza and without it ﴿اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ what you need, He will give you ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا﴾ including the proper place of bounty and your asking

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَلِكُلٍّ﴾ of men and women ﴿جَعَلْنَا مَوَالِيَ﴾ agnatic heirs (ʿaṣaba) who are given ﴿مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوَالِدَانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ﴾ for them, of wealth ﴿وَالَّذِينَ عَاقَدَتْ﴾ with an alif and without it [عَقَدَتْ] ﴿أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ plural of يَمِين, in the sense of oath or hand, i.e. the confederates with whom you made a pact in the Jāhiliyya for support and inheritance ﴿فَآتُوهُمْ﴾ now ﴿نَصِيبَهُمْ﴾ their portions of the inheritance, which is a sixth ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدًا﴾ aware, including your state. This is abrogated by His saying {وَأُولُو الْأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ} ("And those related by blood are more entitled to one another").

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿الرِّجَالُ قَوَّامُونَ﴾ in authority ﴿عَلَى النِّسَاءِ﴾ disciplining them and restraining them ﴿بِمَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ﴾ i.e. by His having preferred them over them in knowledge, intellect, guardianship and other things ﴿وَبِمَا أَنْفَقُوا﴾ on them ﴿مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ فَالصَّالِحَاتُ﴾ among them ﴿قَانِتَاتٌ﴾ obedient to their husbands ﴿حَافِظَاتٌ لِلْغَيْبِ﴾ i.e. guarding their chastity and other things in their husbands' absence ﴿بِمَا حَفِظَ﴾ them ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ in that He enjoined the husbands concerning them ﴿وَالَّتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ﴾ their disobedience to you, its signs having appeared [Translator's note: the source text writes the Quranic word as وَالَّتِي; the muṣḥaf reads وَاللَّاتِي.] ﴿فَعِظُوهُنَّ﴾ make them fear Allah ﴿وَاهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِي الْمَضَاجِعِ﴾ withdraw to another bed if they show recalcitrance ﴿وَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ﴾ a non-injurious beating, if they do not return through the desertion ﴿فَإِنْ أَطَعْنَكُمْ﴾ in what is wanted from them ﴿فَلَا تَبْغُوا﴾ seek ﴿عَلَيْهِنَّ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way to beat them wrongfully ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيًّا كَبِيرًا﴾ so beware of Him punishing you if you wrong them

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ﴾ you know ﴿شِقَاقَ﴾ disagreement ﴿بَيْنِهِمَا﴾ between the spouses; the genitive construct (iḍāfa) is by extension (li-l-ittisāʿ), i.e. a discord between them ﴿فَابْعَثُوا﴾ to them, with their consent ﴿حَكَمًا﴾ an upright man ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِهِ﴾ his relatives ﴿وَحَكَمًا مِنْ أَهْلِهَا﴾ The husband appoints his arbiter as his agent for divorce and for accepting compensation for it, and she appoints her arbiter as her agent for khulʿ; they exert their effort and command the wrongdoer to return [Translator's note: to what is right], or separate them if they see fit. He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنْ يُرِيدَا﴾ i.e. the two arbiters ﴿إِصْلَاحًا يُوَفِّقِ اللَّهُ بَيْنَهُمَا﴾ between the spouses, i.e. He enables them to do what is obedience, whether reconciliation or separation ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا﴾ of everything ﴿خَبِيرًا﴾ of the inward as of the outward
